title: Kummer and diagonal classes of towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_{\bullet,T}=((\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T)_{n\geq1}$ and $A_{\bullet,T}=((\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T)_{n\geq1}$, with quotient transitions, for every scheme $T$ over $S$. Use the topos of inverse systems and its module category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and its ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $A_{\bullet,T}(1)=(\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T)_n$, with the power and quotient transitions; its inverse line tower is denoted $A_{\bullet,T}(-1)$, consistently with [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. The roots of unity and their power transitions are those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf].

1. In towers of abelian sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n\longrightarrow(\mathbf G_{m,S},(\cdot)^\ell)\xrightarrow{((\cdot)^{\ell^n})_n}(\mathbf G_{m,S},\mathrm{id})\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$; the middle tower has power-$\ell$ transitions, and the last tower has identity transitions.
2. A line bundle $L$ (an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]) has its line-bundle class in $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbf Z_S,\mathbf G_{m,S})$. Its constant-tower image has a boundary in $\operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S},(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n)$ for the sequence in (1), where $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}$ is the constant tower. This boundary has a canonical coefficient-linear realization
$$R_{\bullet,S}\longrightarrow(\mu_{\ell^n,S})_n[2]$$
in the derived category of $R_{\bullet,S}$-modules in the inverse-system topos: apply derived extension $R_{\bullet,S}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}}-$ to the constant-tower line-bundle morphism $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}\to\mathbf G_{m,S}[1]$. After forgetting scalars and precomposing with the canonical quotient $\mathbf Z_{\bullet,S}\to R_{\bullet,S}$, this morphism is the preceding abelian boundary. Extension along $R_{\bullet,S}\to A_{\bullet,S}$ defines
$$c_1(L):A_{\bullet,S}\longrightarrow A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(S,\mathcal O_E))$, whose evaluation at $n$ is the finite Kummer first Chern class with coefficients $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$.
3. Put $P=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)=\mathbf P^1_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_SP$, and let $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal Cartier divisor, with $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$ defined by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Put $B=\nu_W^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$ and let $a:B\to\mathbf G_{m,W}$ be the canonical units comparison, induced by restriction to etale charts [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use the pulled-back Cartier extension $0\to B\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P\to0$ with quotient $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$ for a local equation $t$ [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. For $C_\Delta=[B\to\mathcal M_\Delta]$ in degrees $-1,0$, write $v:C_\Delta\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P$ for the quotient quasi-isomorphism and $p:C_\Delta\to B[1]$ for the positive projection. Take the image of its connecting morphism $\beta_\Delta=a[1](-p v^{-1}):\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P\to\mathbf G_{m,W}[1]$, using the same cone convention as in (2), and apply the same derived coefficient extension and target identification as in (2) to $\beta_\Delta$. This defines
$$\delta_\bullet:\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}\longrightarrow A_{\bullet,W}(1)[2]$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(W,\mathcal O_E))$, whose evaluation at $n$ is the finite diagonal class. Its composite with $A_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}$ is $c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$.
4. For $q:P\to S$, let $Rq_{*,\bullet}$ be the proper tower direct image of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The unit and $c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, where $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is the hyperplane line bundle obtained on affine base opens from [def-pc-projective-space-twist], give an isomorphism
$$b_q:A_{\bullet,S}\oplus A_{\bullet,S}(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{*,\bullet}A_{\bullet,P}.$$
Define the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}:Rq_{*,\bullet}A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2]\to A_{\bullet,S}$ by twisting and shifting $b_q^{-1}$ and projecting onto its second summand. Its evaluation at $n$ is the finite projective-line trace.

proof.text: Kummer exactness on the pro-etale site is a local consequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. For a pro-etale object $U\to S$ and $u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, apply that lemma on the scheme $U$ with exponent $\ell^n$. It supplies an etale cover of $U$ on which $u$ is an $\ell^n$th power. Such a cover is also a cover in the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so the power map on the specified pro-etale units sheaf is an epimorphism. Its kernel is $\mu_{\ell^n}$ by [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Kernels and cokernels of inverse systems are levelwise, as for the system topos in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The maps form a sequence of towers because $(u^\ell)^{\ell^n}=u^{\ell^{n+1}}$, and a root of unity maps to its $\ell$th power. This proves (1); no change-of-site identification of the entire units sheaf is being assumed.

source.place: (1); Stacks Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence, applied on every pro-etale object U

proof.text: Construct the integral class of $L$ before introducing finite coefficients. On a Zariski trivializing cover choose frames $e_a$ of $L$ and let its transition units be defined by $e_b=g_{ab}e_a$, so $g_{ab}g_{bc}=g_{ac}$. The section $(u,m)_a$ below is to be read as the frame $ue_a^{m}$ of $L^{\otimes m}$; then $ue_b^m=g_{ab}^mue_a^m$ gives the gluing rule, and this direction of the transitions is the one for which the construction is the class of $L$ rather than of $L^{-1}$. Glue the sheaves $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf Z$ with abelian group law $(u,m)(v,k)=(uv,m+k)$ by $(u,m)_b\mapsto(g_{ab}^{m}u,m)_a$. The cocycle identity gives the gluing identity; the kernel at $m=0$ is $\mathbf G_m$, and the projection to $m$ is locally split. Thus this explicitly constructs an extension $0\to\mathbf G_m\to E_L\to\mathbf Z\to0$ on the pro-etale site. Its connecting morphism $\lambda_L:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf G_m[1]$ exists and is the extension class by [lem-weil-pbc-ext-one-extension-classification]. Changing frames gives an isomorphic extension fixing endpoints. On the etale site the identical construction is precisely the line-bundle torsor class, by the named construction in [lem-sc-torsor-h1] and the line-bundle/torsor correspondence [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]; both statements allow arbitrary schemes. Hence the pro-etale extension just written fixes the same Kummer sign and convention, without assuming a pro-etale Picard comparison theorem. Taking constant towers is exact (all kernels and cokernels are levelwise), so the constant extension and its connecting morphism define the line-bundle class in the tower category.

source.place: (2), integral line-bundle class; Stacks Tags 03AJ and 06XV

proof.text: Make coefficient linearity part of the construction. Let $\mathscr X$ be the topos of inverse systems of sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ supplied by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on a site presenting this topos to the ring map $\mathbf Z_\bullet\to R_\bullet$. It gives the exact functor $T_R(K)=R_\bullet\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_\bullet}\operatorname{const}(K)$ with values in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_\bullet}(\mathscr X))$, not merely in abelian systems. To check its evaluations, choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The constant-system functor is inverse image of a geometric morphism: it preserves finite limits and is left adjoint to inverse limit. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] it preserves these K-flat resolutions. Constant flat terms remain flat since tensor and exactness of systems are componentwise. Thus a single model $P\otimes R_\bullet$ computes $T_R(K)$ and all evaluations $P\otimes\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The evaluation isomorphisms commute with transitions because the latter maps are the actual quotient maps in this model.

proof.text: Compute the target of $T_R(\lambda_L)$. After forgetting the new scalar action, resolve $R_\bullet$ by the two-term system $Q_n=[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transition $(\ell,1):Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. Each term is a flat system (tensor and exactness are levelwise). This bounded complex is K-flat directly: tensoring with any acyclic system is the cone of a map between two acyclic systems, hence acyclic. Therefore the K-flat tensor construction of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes the underlying $T_R(\mathbf G_m)$ by $[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf G_m]_n$. By the Kummer-exactness step its only cohomology is $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$ in degree $-1$, with transition $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. Use the positive kernel inclusion $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[1]\to[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf G_m]_n$ for this cohomology identification. Define the identification $T_R(\mathbf G_m[1])\simeq(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[2]$ by shifting this identification through the exact functor's shift isomorphism; this fixes its sign. These are identifications inside the module derived category: canonical truncation identifies an object with its unique nonzero cohomology, and [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] identifies that cohomology's level-$n$ action with its unique $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ action. Also $T_R(\mathbf Z)=R_\bullet$. Apply $T_R$ to $\lambda_L$ to obtain the stated $R_\bullet$-linear Chern morphism.

proof.text: Check the abelian boundary, rather than identifying arbitrary abelian Ext with module Ext. The ordinary tensor units of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] on K-flat resolutions define a natural map from a complex to the scalar-forgotten derived extension: for a K-flat resolution $P\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ use the roof $K\xleftarrow{\sim}P\to P\otimes R_\bullet$; naturality and independence follow from the resolution comparisons in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

proof.text: Check its sign first before shifting. Write $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{f}N\to0$ for the Kummer tower sequence of the Kummer-exactness step, so $U=(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$, $M$ has power transitions, and $N$ has identity transitions. Set $C=[U\xrightarrow{i}M]$ and $D=[M\xrightarrow{f}N]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The augmentation $v:C\to N$ is $f$ in degree zero, and the cone projection is $p:C\to U[1]$. With the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], the boundary is $\delta=-p v^{-1}$. Let $a:N\to D$ be the degree-zero inclusion and $j:U[1]\to D$ the positive kernel inclusion. The map $av+jp:C\to D$ is null-homotopic: take the sole nonzero homotopy $h^0=1_M:C^0\to D^{-1}$; then $d_Dh+hd_C$ has components $i$ in degree $-1$ and $f$ in degree zero. Hence $j^{-1}a=-pv^{-1}=\delta$ in the derived category of abelian systems. In the model $N\otimes Q$ of the two-term target-computation step, the tensor unit is precisely $a$. Shift this equality using the target normalization fixed in the two-term target-computation step to obtain $\delta[1]$ for $\mathbf G_m[1]$. The homotopy is a map of entire systems, since its middle term has the power transitions on both sides.

proof.text: Naturality of the tensor unit gives $\operatorname{Res}(T_R(\lambda_L))\circ(\mathbf Z_\bullet\to R_\bullet)=\delta[1]\circ\operatorname{const}(\lambda_L)$. Thus precomposition with the integral generator realizes the Chern morphism as the boundary in (2). Evaluation gives the identical formula for the finite Kummer boundary, with the same transition $(\ell,1)$ on its two-term models. The scalar-extension adjunction is used in the abelian sheaf setting of the integral and scalar-extension constructions, where finite colimits exist; the revised finite-colimit proviso for right exactness imposes no additional hypothesis here.

proof.text: Extend $T_R(\lambda_L)$ along $R_\bullet\to A_\bullet$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], on the same inverse-system topos. This constructs an $A_\bullet$-linear morphism, and evaluation computes finite scalar extension by the K-flat model argument of the K-flat scalar-extension step; the source becomes $A_\bullet$. Apply [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free](1) with $X=S$ and the fixed prime $\ell$ and extension $E$, choosing an auxiliary algebraic closure containing $E$ as in that node's preamble. Its clause (1) supplies one pro-etale cover $\widetilde S\to S$ and generators $\zeta_n$ with $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$. The maps $a\mapsto\zeta_n^a$ identify the entire root tower with $R_\bullet$ on that cover: the transition sends $\zeta_{n+1}^a$ to $\zeta_n^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a$ is reduction modulo $\ell^n$. Thus the root tower is locally free of rank one over $R_\bullet$, and tensoring with it is exact because exactness and tensor are computed levelwise. Its derived extension is therefore the degree-zero tower $A_\bullet(1)$, and its dual is the inverse line tower. At each level the finite ring $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ is commutative and killed by $\ell^n$; taking $A=A_n$ and $r=n$ is precisely the finite-coefficient convention of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], where finite discrete coefficient rings have constant coefficient sheaves. Its displayed $B_{E,n}$ is this $A_n$, and its transition $u\otimes a\mapsto u^\ell\otimes\bar a$ is exactly the transition of our $A_\bullet(1)$. The isomorphism of clause (2) of [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] also identifies any larger annihilating level with this one. No assertion about the integral, rational or algebraically closed bounded constructible categories in that node's revised clause (3) is used. Step 7 evaluated at $n$ is now the finite scalar-extended Kummer class, proving all of (2), with the power transitions on roots and quotient transitions on coefficients.

proof.text: Fix $W=P\times_SP$ and $F=\Delta_*\mathbf Z_P$. In the current statement of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system], the units in the exact pole extension are $B=\nu_W^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$, rather than the sheaf $G=\mathbf G_{m,W}$ of all pro-etale units. Let $a:B\to G$ be the map adjoint to the identity on units on etale objects, using [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Clause (1) supplies $0\to B\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to F\to0$, with $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$. Put $C_\Delta=[B\to\mathcal M_\Delta]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with quotient quasi-isomorphism $v:C_\Delta\to F$ and positive projection $p:C_\Delta\to B[1]$. By the cone convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] its connecting morphism is $\beta_B=-pv^{-1}$. Define $\beta_\Delta=a[1]\beta_B$. Clause (3) of the diagonal-system statement supplies only the source reduction $T(F)\simeq\Delta_*R_\bullet$ used below. We do not use its target-system identification or clause (4). The target normalization is fixed by the two-term computation; the finite Cartier comparison is applied below.

proof.text: Check the normalization directly. Let $\rho:\mathbf Z_W\to F$ send $1$ to $1$ on the diagonal. On etale charts with equations $t_b=g_{ab}^{-1}t_a$, the lifts $s_a=t_a^{-1}$ have ratios $s_b/s_a=g_{ab}$, the transitions of $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$. The pullback of the pole extension along $\rho$ is locally $B\times\mathbf Z$, with $(b,m)_b\mapsto(g_{ab}^m b,m)_a$; the map to the pole sheaf sends $(b,m)$ to $b t_a^{-m}$. This is an isomorphism onto the pullback: a section over a fixed exponent differs from its chosen lift by a unique section of the kernel $B$. The maps $(b,m)\mapsto(a(b),m)$ define a morphism from this extension to the explicitly constructed full-units extension $E_{\mathcal O_W(\Delta)}$ in the integral line-bundle-extension step. They commute with the transitions because $a(g_{ab})=g_{ab}$, and have endpoint maps $a$ and the identity of $\mathbf Z$. Naturality of connecting morphisms, or the commuting maps of the two cones with their negative projections, gives $a[1]\beta_B\rho=\lambda_{\mathcal O_W(\Delta)}$. The endpoint convention is the one in [lem-weil-pbc-ext-one-extension-classification]. No isomorphism $B\simeq G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the module-valued exact functor $T_R$ of the K-flat scalar-extension step to this corrected integral morphism, using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The underlying source reduction is the cited $T(F)$, and it has only degree-zero cohomology $\Delta_*R_\bullet$. Truncation inside the module derived category and the unique levelwise quotient actions of [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] identify the source there. Identify the target with $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[2]$ using exactly the positive-kernel identification and shift normalization of the two-term target-computation step; do not alter that identification for the supported class. This produces the $R_\bullet$-linear supported morphism $T_R(\beta_\Delta)=-T_R(a[1])T_R(\partial)$, where $\partial=pv^{-1}$ is the cited positive roof with target $B[1]$. Applying the additive functor to the preceding integral equality shows that its composite with $R_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*R_{\bullet,P}$ is the Chern morphism of $\mathcal O_W(\Delta)$. All maps are constructed on entire systems before evaluation.

proof.text: Extend the corrected map $T_R(\beta_\Delta)$ from $R_\bullet$ to $A_\bullet$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3), $\mathcal O_E$ is finite free over $\mathbf Z_\ell$; a fixed basis reduces to compatible bases of $A_n$ over $R_n$. Thus $A_\bullet$ is finite free over $R_\bullet$, and its tensor functor is exact levelwise. In such a basis the canonical map $A_\bullet\otimes_{R_\bullet}\Delta_*R_\bullet\to\Delta_*A_\bullet$ is the identity on the corresponding finite direct sum of copies of $\Delta_*R_\bullet$. Step 8 identifies the target as $A_\bullet(1)[2]$. Define $\delta_\bullet$ by this extension, retaining the source and target identifications of the integral supported-class construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-cartier-reduction-site-comparison] with $Z=W$, $D=\Delta$, $r=n$, $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and $\Lambda=A_n$. The ring $A_n$ is finite commutative and killed by $\ell^n$ even for ramified $E$; $\ell$ is invertible on $W$. The compatible charts of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] and their identification with $P$ in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] give chart rings $C[x,y]$ over every affine base $\operatorname{Spec}C$. On equal charts the diagonal equation is $x-y$, monic in $x$. On opposite charts it is $xy-1$; writing $f=\sum f_k(y)x^k$, the equality $(xy-1)f=0$ gives $f_0=0$ and $f_k=yf_{k-1}=0$. Thus both equations are non-zero-divisors over arbitrary base rings. The new lemma identifies evaluation of the entire reduced supported boundary, with precisely the quotient source and positive kernel target fixed above, with the finite Cartier class. Evaluation commutes with scalar extension by the K-flat models already constructed. Applying these additive functors to the integral equality $\beta_\Delta\rho=\lambda_{\mathcal O(\Delta)}$ gives $\delta_\bullet\circ(A_{\bullet,W}\to\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P})=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. This proves clause (3) without inferring equality of supported morphisms from this composite alone.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with the two-element index set $\{0,1\}$, $q:P\to S$ is proper. Use its compactification $q=q\circ\mathrm{id}_P$ when applying [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The coefficient sheaf and its twists and shifts are bounded below, as required by that node's $D^+$ hypothesis. Use the canonical ringed-topos derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] for the levelwise morphism of inverse-system topoi induced by q. The hyperplane line on each affine base open is [def-pc-projective-space-twist] with $d=1$: its frames satisfy $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$. These transition functions commute with restriction on the base, so they glue to the specified $\mathcal O_P(1)$. Form $b_q$ by the tower adjunction unit and the adjoint of the Chern morphism of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, untwisted and shifted on its source. Clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] supplies the bounded-below direct-image comparison. To check evaluation of the actual adjunction maps, apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] with the strict coefficient system $B_n=(A_n)_S$ and the pro-etale inverse image of $q$. The pulled-back coefficient system is $(A_n)_P$, since inverse image preserves constant sheaves. This lemma explicitly preserves evaluation, units, counits, tensor products and adjunction transposes, so the constructed tower unit/Chern map evaluates to the same map over $A_n$. The canonical identification of the pulled-back twist with the twist on $P$ follows from the single compatible-generator cover of the compatible-root trivialization step: its pullback sends each generator to the same root and the local coefficient-line identification to the identity. No unrestricted projection-formula isomorphism from clause (2)(a) is used.

proof.text:
This finite map is invertible without Noetherianity of $S$. Apply [det-sp-p1-trace](1) over $R_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. Its $h$ and twist are pulled back from the etale site by $
u_P^*$. For a line bundle $L$, the step-2 gluing with etale units pulls back to an extension of $\mathbf Z$ by $B=
u^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,\mathrm{et}}$, and $(b,m)\mapsto(a(b),m)$, $a$ as in (3) [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], maps it to $E_L$ fixing $\mathbf Z$, as $a(g_{ab})=g_{ab}$. The naturality in [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] (hypotheses by step 1; $\mathbf Z$ is torsion-free), for this map and exact $
u^{-1}$, carries the pulled etale Kummer class to ours through $
u^{-1}\mu_{\ell^n,\mathrm{et}}	o\mu_{\ell^n}$, an isomorphism fixing etale local generators [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]; the normalization is that of step 6. On restricting $A_n$-modules to $R_n$, $A_n$ is a finite direct sum of $R_n$ in the fixed integral basis. Canonical composition of ringed-topos derived direct images [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] applied to the two factorizations of the coefficient-change square identifies restriction of $Rq_{*,A_n}$ with $Rq_{*,R_n}$ of restriction; exact restriction is its termwise derived functor, as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](4). Thus the restriction of $(b_q)_n$ is the direct sum of these $R_n$ projective-line isomorphisms: on the $j$th basis vector its Chern component is $e_j\otimes c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ by the compatible-root trivialization step, and its unit component is $e_j$ times the unit. Finite direct sums commute with an additive derived direct image. Restriction keeps cohomology sheaves, so it reflects isomorphisms. Hence $(b_q)_n$ is invertible over $A_n$. Finally [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3) implies $b_q$ is invertible in the tower module derived category. For clause (4) of the scalar-change node, the sheaf category is abelian with additive tensor, so its revised clause (2) proviso holds.

proof.text:
Put $V=A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]$, an invertible object with inverse $V^{-1}=A_{\bullet,S}(-1)[-2]$ by the compatible-root trivialization step. Write $L=q^{-1}$ and $R=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ for the derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; its pullback tensor comparison gives $L(V^{-1})=(LV)^{-1}$. For any $M$ and $C$, tensoring by these inverse lines and applying that adjunction gives natural bijections
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(M,RC\otimes V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes V^{-1},RC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LM\otimes LV^{-1},C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LM,C\otimes LV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,R(C\otimes LV)).
$$
The forward map is the counit-tensor transpose specified in the cited node: transpose, cancel the inverse line and transpose back. Running these bijections backwards gives its inverse; their composites are identities by the evaluation/coevaluation cancellations for the line and the adjunction triangle identities. Thus the projection map is invertible for this $V$ over the arbitrary scheme $S$, without applying the restricted general projection theorem of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2)(a). Take $C=A_{\bullet,P}$ and use $LV=A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2]$ from the generator calculation in the unit/Chern-map construction. Tensor $b_q$ with $V$ and compose with this projection isomorphism to obtain $A_{\bullet,S}(1)[2]\oplus A_{\bullet,S}\simeq Rq_{*,\bullet}(A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2])$. Define $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,\bullet}$ to be the second projection after its inverse. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], evaluation preserves the tensor, counit-tensor transpose, adjunctions and compositions in this construction, and it preserves inverses by functoriality. The evaluated splitting is therefore precisely the twist of the finite unit/Chern splitting, so [det-sp-p1-trace](2) identifies its second projection with the finite trace, extended to $A_n$. This proves (4) with the stated trace type.
